    Finite-dimensional division algebras over algebraically closed fields #

    A finite-dimensional central division algebra over an algebraically closed field consists only of scalars. The proof uses an eigenvector of left multiplication and works without first proving that the division algebra is commutative.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.algebraMap_surjective_of_finiteDimensional_divisionRing (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (D : Type v) [DivisionRing D] [Algebra k D] [Module.Finite k D] :
    Function.Surjective ⇑(algebraMap k D)

    The scalar embedding into a finite-dimensional division algebra over an algebraically closed field is surjective.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.exists_sub_algebraMap_mem_ringJacobson (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (R : Type v) [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsDedekindFiniteMonoid R] [IsLocalRing R] (x : R) :
    ∃ (c : k), x - (algebraMap k R) c ∈ Ring.jacobson R

    Every element of a finite-dimensional local algebra over an algebraically closed field is congruent to a scalar modulo its Jacobson radical.
